lists.content: AI Labs is paperWave's bet on what comes after the toolbox era of software. No backlog rituals, no six-month roadmaps, no committees — small teams, weekly ship cycles, real users from day one. We build AI-native products for the businesses that actually run the economy: the contractor booking your kitchen remodel, the dentist scheduling your cleaning, the 10-person shop drowning in W-9s and PDFs nobody designed for them. They've been stuck with decades-old software. We're here to change that, fast.

For thirty years, software gave people toolboxes — edit this, sign that, file the other thing, one click at a time. AI lets us skip the toolbox entirely and hand people the outcome: taxes filed, contracts signed, staff onboarded, done. That's not an incremental upgrade. It's a chance to make our own products — and everyone else's — obsolete, fast. Whoever builds this first wins a category. We want it to be us, and we want it to be you.

You'll own an AI-native product end to end — not manage a backlog, not shepherd someone else's roadmap. You work closely with AI Labs' product leader, who sets the broad direction, but everything from "who is this customer, really" to "why is this metric moving" to "ship it tonight" is yours. You'll have a small team of engineers who are good, fast, and looking to you to make the next six months feel like an adventure instead of a slog.

• Get obsessed with the customer. Talk to SMB owners, watch them work, mine the signal sitting in our millions of existing users — find the problem they actually have, not the one that's convenient for us.

  • Run on hypotheses, not opinions. Form a sharp bet, design the test, read the result honestly even when it stings, move.

  • Own the funnel and the money. Activation, conversion, retention, monetization — know the numbers cold and push them yourself.

  • Turn mess into a thing worth building. Insight is cheap; a sharp, buildable product decision is not.

  • Build alongside your engineers, not above them. Prototype with AI tools — v0, Cursor, Lovable, whatever's fastest — and fix your own interface instead of filing a ticket for it.

  • Ship in days, not quarters. Idea to something real in front of a user in about a week. Then do it again.

  • Bring the energy that makes people want to build with you. This is the job where "it's just a job" gets you replaced.

• ~3–5 years building software products and shipping V1s that real customers actually used — SMB experience is a strong plus.

  • Customer-obsessed by instinct, not by training — you start from their problem, not our roadmap.

  • AI-native. You use these tools every day, not just on slide decks, and you have sharp instincts for what they can and can't do yet.

  • You've run experiments that mattered — you can name the bet, the test, and what you learned when you were wrong.

  • Curious and genuinely unafraid to be wrong in public. Fast learners who chase the question outrun people who protect their ego.

  • A real nose for product — you can tell good from bad in five minutes, not five meetings.

  • Hands-on by default. Given the choice between a rough prototype and a strategy doc, you build the prototype.

  • Fluent in growth and monetization — funnels, conversion, pricing, the levers that actually move a business, not just a metric.

  • Hungry for freedom on new things — and ready to run with it the moment you get it.

lists.text: Fair warning on how we hire:
lists.content: Before we talk about strategy, we're going to ask you to build something — a real prototype, a few hours of work, not a two-week slog. If that sounds like an annoying hoop, this probably isn't your role. If it sounds like the most fun part of the interview, you're exactly who we're looking for.

lists.text: Why this and not somewhere else:
lists.content: Startup speed and ownership, backed by a company with 100M+ users, real infrastructure, and the resources to actually support what you build — plus direct access to leadership, because this hire is that important to us. You won't wait for permission. You'll build the thing, watch someone use it, and know within a week if you're onto something real.

  • Prioritize against business impact. Make the case for investment in your area, and against work that will not pay off, including your own.

lists.content:
• Delivering product features with AI coding agents as your primary implementation loop: writing specs and context-rich tasks that carry architecture, team standards, existing patterns, and acceptance criteria, then iterating until the output meets the bar

Strategic

  • Own email-channel-driven attributed revenue as a business outcome, setting the strategic direction for how email contributes to LTV, retention, and expansion across paperWave products
  • Define email and push notification strategy in line with product and marketing strategies
  • Lead churn-prevention and win-back initiatives across email and push notifications as coordinated, signal-driven programs rather than one-off campaigns
  • Set the email roadmap for 2026 and beyond — audit existing programs, identify gaps and quick wins, and prioritize initiatives across three products against attributed revenue targets
  • Define how email fits within multi-channel orchestration, establishing boundaries and handoffs between email, in-product messaging, and other channels

    • Data & use of data

    • Translate behavioral signals, predictive churn scores, and lifecycle stage classifications into actionable segmentation logic and program triggers
    • Define data requirements for email programs — specify the user signals, cohort definitions, and event triggers needed from the data engineering team, and own those requests
    • Own the team's contribution to the revenue attribution model — partner with data teams to define lifecycle-stage KPIs and validate that email is correctly credited under the new attribution framework
    • Own email dashboards with the data team and align them with lifecycle dashboards, so attribution reporting accurately reflects email's contribution to revenue at each funnel stage
    • Use generative and agentic AI tooling to drive personalization and automation at scale across a large, multi-product subscriber base

      • Operational

      • Manage and develop three email marketing specialists — set priorities, coach on execution quality, and connect daily work to strategic lifecycle goals
      • Coordinate across the email development team, data team, demand gen, and product stakeholders to deliver lifecycle programs end-to-end within airEML
      • Maintain and evolve automated email journeys across all four products, with the authority to rebuild or retire programs where data supports it
      • Ensure email deliverability and list health at scale across a large, multi-product subscriber base

• 5+ years in email marketing as a senior contributor or leader, retention marketing, or lifecycle marketing with an email focus — B2C or B2B SaaS/subscription products at scale preferred

  • Experience using behavioral data and predictive models for segmentation, such as churn scoring or lifecycle stage classification

  • A track record of cross-functional collaboration with Product and Data Science teams, not siloed within Marketing
  • Strategic thinking at the program level, not only the campaign level
  • Strong analytical skills, including comfort with dashboards and data-warehouse-sourced data, and the ability to derive lifecycle insights independently
  • Understanding of email deliverability and list health at scale (100K+ subscriber base)
  • A Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Upper-Intermediate (B2) or higher English, written and spoken
• Experience in a multi-product or multi-brand environment

lists.content:
Own product positioning and messaging

  • Develop and continuously refine positioning, messaging and value propositions for pdfFiller across key customer segments and use cases.
  • Translate complex product capabilities, including AI-powered functionality, into clear customer benefits and compelling commercial narratives.
  • Ensure our positioning is differentiated, evidence-based and consistently reflected across the customer journey.

    •  

    Lead go-to-market strategy

  • Own the product marketing strategy for major launches, new capabilities and strategic initiatives from early planning through adoption.
  • Define target audiences, use cases, value propositions, competitive differentiation, launch plans and success measures.
  • Partner with Product early in the development process so customer and market insight informs what we build, not simply how we market it after launch.

    •  

    Develop deep customer and market insight

  • Build a strong understanding of pdfFiller customers, prospects, competitors and broader document productivity market.
  • Conduct customer research, win/loss analysis, competitive analysis and market segmentation to identify opportunities and inform Product and GTM strategy.
  • Turn customer insight and market data into recommendations leaders can act on.

    •  

    Drive adoption and commercial impact

  • Partner with Growth and Lifecycle Marketing to improve activation, adoption, conversion, retention and expansion.
  • Identify gaps between product capability and customer understanding and develop strategies to close them.
  • Use data to evaluate whether positioning, launches and campaigns are changing customer behavior and contributing to business outcomes.

    •  

    Enable Sales and customer-facing teams

  • Create sales narratives, competitive intelligence, battlecards, customer stories, presentations and other enablement materials that help customer-facing teams communicate pdfFiller's value effectively.
  • Partner directly with Sales to understand objections, competitive pressure and customer needs and bring those insights back into Product and Marketing.

    •  

    Shape product strategy

  • Represent the voice of the market in product discussions.
  • Partner with Product leaders to evaluate market opportunities, customer problems, competitive dynamics and potential areas of investment.
  • Help the organization answer not only "Can we build this?" but "Who is this for, what problem does it solve, and why will customers choose us?"

  • Demonstrated ownership of product positioning, messaging and go-to-market strategy

  • Experience bringing new products or major capabilities to market

  • Strong understanding of SaaS customer journeys, including acquisition, activation, conversion, retention and expansion

  • Experience partnering closely with Product, Sales, Growth and other cross-functional teams

  • Strong customer research, market analysis and competitive intelligence capabilities

  • Ability to turn complex technology into simple, compelling customer value

  • Strong commercial judgment and comfort using data to make decisions

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

  • Ability to operate independently in a distributed, international organization

lists.text: What you will be working on:
lists.content:
• Continue to drive digital marketing performance, expanding from search to under-used channels — display, social, video, community, and more. Optimize our $50M+ marketing budget to improve overall ROI across all products in terms of CAC/LTV.

  • Build proper multichannel campaigns with supporting assets that convey the value of our products to our ICPs, rather than optimizing each channel in isolation on bottom-of-funnel metrics alone. You'll partner closely with each BU's product marketing managers to sharpen and bring their positioning to life in these campaigns.

  • Build and scale a real B2B demand-gen engine — lead gen, scoring, and routing — in partnership with sales, growing the small team already exploring this area today.

  • Raise the bar on content strategy and execution across every surface and channel, including web.

  • Build our martech stack in partnership with our VP of Engineering, making build-vs-buy calls that reserve first-party engineering capacity for our most uniquely proprietary needs.

  • Build the data instrumentation, reporting, and dashboards our new marketing campaigns and channels require, in partnership with the data team.

  • Act as a trusted partner to our GMs on GTM strategy, especially positioning, competitive differentiation, and ICP definition.

• A seasoned marketing executive with 15–20 years of experience in SaaS.

  • A proven track record straddling self-serve digital execution and scaled, sales-assisted motion with large SMB/mid-market accounts (this role is not enterprise field marketing). Direct experience building and scaling B2B demand gen — lead gen, scoring, routing — in close partnership with sales is critical.

  • Hands-on: a "do it yourself until you delegate" builder. We expect the leader to develop much of this new muscle themselves, scrappily and with skinny teams, before scaling it.

  • AI-first, culturally — in how we work, the martech tools we use, and new AI-driven channels we can leverage, like GAO.

  • Strong cross-functional operator, comfortable working closely with sales and business units across a multi-brand portfolio.

  • Balanced strengths across execution and strategy, with a proven edge in positioning-led demand creation.

  • Fast, decisive, and willing to test and fail — while staying humble and low-ego. Comfortable with ambiguity, since you'll inherit a team that's still only half built out.

• Affinity for SMBs, especially micro and small businesses.

  • Prior exposure to the document space is a plus.
